items.topic: Feedforward 3D mapping as a navigation substrate
items.whyItMatters: If a single-pass reconstruction model can produce maps that hold up under navigation, the geometric optimisation loop that most visual navigation stacks depend on becomes optional — which changes what is feasible on-robot.
items.investigating: Benchmarking the DUSt3R / MASt3R / CUT3R lineage against existing visual navigation pipelines, scoring reconstructions by downstream navigation performance rather than geometry metrics alone.
items.progress: Benchmarking sprint in progress at the Robotics Research Center.

items.whyItMatters: Language-conditioned policies are strong at interpreting an instruction and weak at remembering where they have been. Persistent topological structure is the cheapest way to give them that memory.
items.investigating: How VLA/VLM policies behave when a topological graph, built online, is available as queryable spatial memory during long-horizon traversal in unstructured environments.
items.progress: Ongoing at the Robotics Research Center under Prof. Sourav Garg.

items.whyItMatters: Vision underdetermines contact state. Whether simulated touch closes that gap well enough to transfer is the question that decides how much real hardware time the work needs.
items.investigating: 3D-vision and RL policies for a LEAP Hand in Isaac Lab, with tactile signal simulated through TacSL.
items.progress: Model development ongoing at the Robotics Research Center.

items.topic: Hierarchical detection of political question evasion
items.whyItMatters: Evasion is structured — a non-answer fails in a specific way — and a hierarchy that respects that structure should beat flat classification over the same labels.
items.investigating: A hierarchical classification system over the QEvasion benchmark for SemEval-2026 Task 6 (CLARITY), as team Nier_ANLP.
items.progress: Shared task selected; system paper in preparation.
